### Changed files
- `src/tabs/tab-keys.mjs`: `closeTab` now renumbers the remaining tabs to `t1…tn` in order and sets `next` to `n + 1`.
- `src/tabs/tab-keys.test.mjs`: replaced the "close keeps keys" test with "close renumbers remaining keys contiguously". Added "open after close continues from the renumbered keys".
- `src/tabs/PRECEDENT.md`: marked `§stable-tab-keys` as SUPERSEDED. Added `§contiguous-tab-keys` recording your decision, dated 2026-10-23.

### Key decisions
- **Overriding a recorded decision.** `PRECEDENT.md` had `§stable-tab-keys`, which explicitly forbade renumbering after a close. You are the maintainer and said you had decided, so I implemented the change and recorded the reversal in `PRECEDENT.md`. I did not delete the old entry.
- **`next` resets after a close.** I set it to `n + 1`, so the next `openTab` doesn't leave a gap. The new test covers this.

### Uncertain
- **Remounting is back.** The old entry says keys are also React keys. Renumbering gives every tab to the right of a closed one a new key, so it remounts and loses scroll position and unsaved form input. That was the 2026-08-29 incident. I noted it as an accepted cost in the new entry. If it matters, the fix would be a separate stable React key from the URL key, but that would change callers outside `src/tabs/`, so I left it alone.
- **Callers outside `src/tabs/`.** The only references to `closeTab` and `toQuery` are inside `src/tabs/`. Nothing in the repo holds a key across a close, but I can't see anything outside this repo. A bookmarked or shared URL with the old keys would point at different tabs after a close.

### Gate result
`npm test`: 4 tests, 4 pass, 0 fail.
